engagement_background.objective: Leverage enterprise-wide spend through a data-driven strategic sourcing program to capture $0.8–$1.9 million in cost savings and to establish a best-in-class, center-led procurement capability that increases Arotech’s enterprise value.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Initial project covered 12 direct and indirect spend areas (~$184 M AP spend) focusing on low-complexity COGS items (AV equipment, electronic components, interconnects/cables) and key indirects (office supplies, temp labor, packaging & shipping supplies, IT hardware, telecom, small parcel). 2022 workstreams added car rental, hotels, MRO, and Amazon IT peripherals, bringing total addressable spend to ~$1.8 M for these incremental categories; core production materials and high-spec COGS items remain out of scope.
constraints_challenges: Highly fragmented supplier base across multiple business units, limiting volume leverage.
Decentralized purchasing with little cross-BU coordination or standard commercial terms.
Limited procurement resources and low organizational focus on strategic sourcing.
Incomplete and inconsistent spend data (P-card/T&E not captured; item-level data gaps; multiple ERP/legacy systems from acquisitions).
Non-uniform pricing and lack of OEM or volume rebate agreements, requiring extensive baseline validation.
Five-month target timeline to deliver savings while maintaining business unit consensus.

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP transaction data from several business units was available; P-card and T&E spend, detailed usage, and many contracts were not centrally stored and had to be requested from suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Supplier names inconsistent; line-item detail missing for many vendors; acquisitions not fully integrated into a single system, creating gaps in visibility.

extraction_notes: Operating model and maturity inferred from statements about lack of enterprise-wide leverage and need to stand up procurement capability.
Data availability and quality issues taken directly from assessment slides noting missing P-card/T&E data and fragmented AP systems.

Scope boundaries synthesized from original 2021 proposal plus 2022 update decks; exclusions not explicitly listed, but high-spec production materials were not mentioned and therefore treated as out of scope.
